summary: Documentation change to docs/kubernetes.md's section 'Running a workload in the cluster from a role' (title unchanged), four corrections in docs/kubernetes.md and skills/legion-worker/references/tools.md (regenerate packages/claude-envoy/legion with bun run build), and one sentence of the LEGION-578 solutions note. Every banked finding was checked against main 3ff60972 and the applied cluster in planning: F1, F2, F4-F7, F9, F10, F12-F18 stand and are fixed (F12 by keeping python3, departure D1); F3 and F11 are overtaken; F8 is resolved by a foreground delete plus an explicit Service wait; F19 is recorded as latent, not fixed, as the release note directs.
planningMeasurements: 2026-10-25 10:38Z planner role container: POD_NAMESPACE unset; command -v psql redis-cli sqlite3 nc dig -> none; python3 present; packages/daemon sets POD_NAMESPACE nowhere.
2026-10-25 10:38Z published reachability block against a never-created Service name: 60 s, 'never answered: gaierror: [Errno -2] Name or service not known', exit 1.

2026-10-25 10:40-10:45Z labelled busybox Job + admitted Service, nothing listening on 5432, check with one print per attempt: pod Ready -> every attempt ConnectionRefusedError for 60.7 s; pod exited (Failed) -> every attempt ConnectionRefusedError for 60.7 s. The cluster refuses both when nothing listens and when the Service has no running pod.

The bash tool is not a bash process ($$ is omp): a trap typed into it never fires at the sequence's end; a bare EXIT trap did not run on SIGTERM/SIGHUP in a quick probe. The sequence must run as its own bash, and its traps are measured in T0.
Service ownerReference must carry blockOwnerDeletion absent or false (deployment admission), so a foreground Job delete does not wait for the Service.
jj snapshot.max-new-file-size = 1MiB; role container has go, flock, openssl, no docker, no psql; nine volume variables set.
tasks: T0 measure first: trap form under set -euo pipefail and INT/TERM/HUP in a bash started from the bash tool, during kubectl wait and the check; Ready-wait behaviour for a server that exits on its own configuration; foreground delete duration and Service wait.

findings.finding: G1 fail-fast cleanup deletes the objects before the log and targetPort can be read; a server dying before Ready exits at the Ready wait
findings.answer: T5 trap prints the pod line, log tail and Service port->targetPort before deleting, preserving the status; T0(b) measures where a pre-Ready failure shows and T7 says so; V2/V3 check it.

findings.finding: G2 the namespace fix overrides the release note's 'record as latent'
findings.answer: Plan records F19 (T3) and adds no -n; recovery and diagnostic commands use the same default namespace as the sequence.

findings.finding: G3 readings stated as exclusive diagnoses; final line is the last attempt only
findings.answer: T7 states each reading as the next thing to check and says the final line reports only the last attempt.

findings.finding: G4 'deleted on any stop short of SIGKILL' is stronger than the traps establish; shell unspecified
findings.answer: T0(a) measures the trap form in a bash the block starts (the bash tool is not a bash process); T5 bounds the promise to the measured cases; V6/V7 check handled and unhandled stops; recovery line for the rest.

findings.finding: G5 private values in heredocs and quoted output
findings.answer: Placeholders stay exactly the issue key, the label line and the compute-class line; the driver substitutes them from a private file under TMPDIR; V14 sweep with counts only; quoted output scrubbed.

findings.answer: T15 written last from V1-V8 captures; old bullets 'as published then'; each 'not run again since' entry rechecked.

findings.answer: Foreground delete plus kubectl wait --for=delete service; listing by name with --ignore-not-found after the waits; quota read V8.

findings.answer: All five clients now checked; T3/T6 scope claims to the measured containers and to packages/daemon's source, not the fleet or the digest.

specDepartures.spec: The section's one worked example, a twenty-line inline python3 loop, can be the thing a reader would actually type once the worker image carries psql.
specDepartures.plan: Keep the python3 reachability check and add no psql example; the check prints a reading per failure class.
specDepartures.evidence: 2026-10-25 10:38Z, a role container of this deployment: command -v psql redis-cli sqlite3 nc dig found none, so a psql example could not be driven from a role container, which the spec's second acceptance bullet and the release note require; python3 runs on every digest and names the failure class the readings key on.
